sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
விகட சக்ர விநாயகா என் ஜீவ
சகட விக்ன நாசகா விரைந்து வா
sections.translit:
vikata chakra vinAyakA en jIva
sakata vigna nAsakA viraindhu vA
sections.en: Vikata Chakra Vinayaka, you are the one who crushes obstacles in the wheel of my life. Please hasten.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
குதித்து வா என்னை மதித்து வா உமையுடல்
உதித்தவா (உன்) திருவடி சிரமதில் பதித்து வா
sections.translit:
kudhitthu vA ennai madhitthu vA umaiyudal
udhitthavA (un) thiruvadi siramadhil padhitthu vA
sections.en: Come dancing joyfully. Come here with grace and regard for me. You, who were born from Parvati’s own form, come and place your divine feet upon my head.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
ஆழியில் உறங்கிடும் அரங்கனையும் நொடி
நாழியில் குனிந்தெழச் செய்த குறும்பா
பாரிடை அடியவர் பணிந்திட முறை செய்தவா
சீருடை கலைகள் யாவும் நேரிடை அருள வா
sections.translit:
Azhiyil uRangidum aranganaiyum nodi
nAzhiyil kunindhezhach cheydha kuRumbA
pAridai adiyavar paNindhida muRai seydhavA
sIrudai kalaigaL yAvum nEridai aruLa vA
sections.en: You are the playful Lord who made even your uncle Vishnu, who is accustomed to resting comfortably in the milky ocean, pinch his ears, bow, and rise again and again. Through this, you established a sacred way for your devotees to worship you. Please come in person and bless your devotees with all the renowned arts of the universe.

notes: The first line in the pallavi is a reference to the Ganesha in Ekambreswarar Temple in Kancheepuram. Kachiyappa Sivachchariar prays to Vikata Chakra Vinayagar in the first verse of his immortal composition, Kandha puranam. “திகட சக்கரச் செம்முக மைந்துளான் சகட சக்கரத் தாமரை நாயகன் அகட சக்கரை வின்மணி யாவூரை விகட சக்கரான் மெய்பதம் போற்றுவாம்”. For a complete version of Sivachchariar’s poetry in English, see below: Kacchiyappa Sivachariar’s Poetry There are several stories about this Ganesha and his name. One of the author’s favorite stories is narrated by Mahaperiyava. தெய்வத்தின் குரல், ஜகத்குரு ஶ்ரீ காஞ்சி காமகோடி பீடாதீச்வர ஶ்ரீ சந்திரசேகரேந்திர சரஸ்வதி சங்கராசாரிய ஸ்வாமிகளின் அருள் வாக்குகள், 1.29 – விகட சக்ர விநாயகர், ஆறாம் பகுதி, பக்கம் 106 -107, வானதி பதிப்பகம், 13, தீனதயாளு தெரு. தி. நகர், சென்னை – 17. In brief, Lord Vishnu brought gifts for his nephew on his birthday. Ganesha did not like any of them. Suddenly, he grabbed the Sudharsana Chakra from his uncle’s hand and swallowed it. With all his pleading in vain, Vishnu resorted to pinching his own ears with his hands, bending down a few times and getting up. This clownish dance of the uncle made Ganesha laugh out loud. The chakra fell and Vishnu picked it up. Such a clownish act became the standard practice to worship Ganesha and the deity acquired the new name, Vikata Chakra Vinayaka. Since Ganesha tricked his uncle to perform a clownish act by holding his chakra, the name was justified. This version of the story is included in the charanam of this song. The legends of Sri Ekambranathar temple are different in regards to Vikata Chakra Vinayagar and the way the name came about. The lore describes Lord Vishnu during Dhaksha Yagna throwing his chakra at Veerabhadra, who was causing havoc at the yagna site. The discus fell on Veerabhadra’s garland of skeletons. One of the skeletons swallowed the chakra. Vishnu sent Ganesha to retrieve it. Vinayaka did a clownish dance by closing his ears with his hands, bending his knees, and getting up a few times. The skeleton in the garland could not take it and laughed out loud. The chakra fell and Vinayaka picked it up. The funny dancing Vinayaka with the chakra became Vikata Chakra Vinayaka. Remember that the Tamil word for clown is Vikata. Veerabhadra and Vikata Chakra Vinayaka
